beats.say: And you grow back every night.
A little. Your spine has soft discs between the bones.
beats.cap: A LITTLE. | YOUR SPINE HAS | SOFT *DISCS* | BETWEEN THE BONES.

beats.say: During the day, gravity squeezes them.
At night, lying down lets them spread out again.
beats.cap: AT NIGHT, | LYING DOWN LETS THEM | *SPREAD OUT* AGAIN.

beats.say: So you're about one centimetre taller in the morning.
beats.cap: SO YOU'RE ABOUT | *1 CM* TALLER | IN THE MORNING.

sources.fact: Spinal cartilage compresses during the day by about 1 cm on average and decompresses when lying down, so you are taller in the morning

math.note: about 1 cm daily height change (University of Illinois MechSE)

post.instagram_caption:
You shrink every single day 📏

The soft discs in your spine get squeezed by gravity during the day and spread out again while you sleep.

That makes you about 1 cm taller in the morning.

Sources: University of Illinois MechSE.
